nodes.description: Oral high-affinity transthyretin tetramer stabilizer, FDA-approved disease-modifying therapy for ATTR cardiomyopathy; binds TTR and prevents dissociation into amyloidogenic monomers.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and Safety of Acoramidis in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: In patients with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, the receipt of acoramidis resulted in a significantly better four-step primary hierarchical outcome containing components of mortality, morbidity, and function than placebo.

nodes.description: Extracellular deposition of Congo-red-positive, apple-green-birefringent fibrillar amyloid in affected tissues is the defining histopathological hallmark of all amyloidoses.

evidence.reference_title: [Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis of amyloidosis: Part 1/3 Year 2020].
evidence.snippet: Confirmation in the tissue by biopsy and Congo red staining with the characteristic green birefringence under polarized light is recommended.

nodes.description: Misfolded precursors polymerize into cross-beta-sheet amyloid fibrils that accumulate extracellularly in precursor-specific target tissues. Progressive deposits disrupt tissue architecture; precursor-specific soluble species may add direct cellular toxicity. The downstream organ effects are therefore modeled separately and retain subtype-specific evidence.
nodes.id: Amyloid Fibril Formation and Extracellular Deposition

evidence.reference_title: Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy-2025 Update: Current Diagnostic Approaches and Emerging Therapeutic Options.
evidence.snippet: Transthyretin-related (ATTR) amyloidosis is a progressive, multisystem disease caused by the extracellular deposition of misfolded transthyretin (TTR) monomers as insoluble amyloid fibrils.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanisms and pathology of protein misfolding and aggregation.
evidence.snippet: Multiple lines of evidence suggest that small soluble species are responsible for the observed toxicity. These species have been associated with numerous detrimental effects, such as permeabilization of cellular membranes, impairment of degradation pathways, disruption of synaptic signalling and mitochondrial dysfunction

evidence.reference_title: Amyloid Neuropathy: From Pathophysiology to Treatment in Light-Chain Amyloidosis and Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis.
evidence.snippet: Amyloid fibrils deposit in the endoneurium of peripheral nerves, often extensive in the dorsal root ganglia and sympathetic ganglia, leading to atrophy of Schwann cells in proximity to amyloid fibrils

nodes.description: Length-dependent autonomic neuropathy from amyloid deposition in autonomic fibers and ganglia produces orthostatic hypotension, gastrointestinal dysmotility, neurogenic bladder, and sexual dysfunction; a life-threatening hallmark of ATTRv amyloidosis.

evidence.reference_title: Familial amyloid polyneuropathy.
evidence.snippet: TTR FAP typically causes a nerve length-dependent polyneuropathy that starts in the feet with loss of temperature and pain sensations, along with life-threatening autonomic dysfunction leading to cachexia and death

nodes.description: Infiltrative cardiomyopathy from amyloid deposition in the myocardium causes wall thickening, restrictive physiology, and progressive heart failure; prominent in AL and ATTR amyloidosis.

evidence.reference_title: The genetics of cardiac amyloidosis.
evidence.snippet: It results from the accumulation of the misfolded protein transthyretin within the myocardium, resulting in amyloid transthyretin-associated cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM).

evidence.reference_title: Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy-2025 Update: Current Diagnostic Approaches and Emerging Therapeutic Options.
evidence.snippet: Clinical manifestations vary widely and may include cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), polyneuropathy (ATTR-PN), or mixed phenotypes.

nodes.description: Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome from amyloid deposition in the flexor retinaculum/tenosynovium is a common early and often presenting sign of ATTRv amyloidosis, frequently predating systemic diagnosis by years.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis: a comprehensive review with a focus on peripheral neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: CTS occurred in two-thirds of patients with ATTRv

nodes.description: In AL amyloidosis, a clonal CD38-positive plasma-cell population produces an amyloidogenic immunoglobulin light chain. This is an acquired clonal precursor-supply mechanism and is not the mechanism of ATTR or AA disease.

evidence.reference_title: Daratumumab-Based Treatment for Immunoglobulin Light-Chain Amyloidosis.
evidence.snippet: Systemic immunoglobulin light-chain (AL) amyloidosis is characterized by deposition of amyloid fibrils of light chains produced by clonal CD38+ plasma cells.

nodes.description: Anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody added to bortezomib-cyclophosphamide-dexamethasone (Dara-CyBorD/D-VCd); standard-of-care induction for newly diagnosed AL amyloidosis that depletes the amyloidogenic clonal plasma cells (ANDROMEDA trial).

evidence.reference_title: Daratumumab-Based Treatment for Immunoglobulin Light-Chain Amyloidosis.
evidence.snippet: The percentage of patients who had a hematologic complete response was significantly higher in the daratumumab group than in the control group (53.3% vs. 18.1%)

nodes.description: GalNAc-conjugated, RNase H-dependent antisense oligonucleotide targeting TTR mRNA; an FDA-approved RNA-lowering therapy for hereditary ATTR amyloidosis (polyneuropathy) with cardiomyopathy trials.

evidence.reference_title: RNA Interference Therapeutics for Hereditary Amyloidosis: A Narrative Review of Clinical Trial Outcomes and Future Directions.
evidence.snippet: Four FDA-approved RNAi medications for ATTR polyneuropathy are patisiran, vutrisiran, inotersen, and eplontersen.

nodes.description: 2'-O-methoxyethyl-modified antisense oligonucleotide that triggers RNase H1-mediated degradation of TTR mRNA, lowering both wild-type and mutant transthyretin; licensed for hereditary ATTR polyneuropathy.

evidence.reference_title: RNA Targeting and Gene Editing Strategies for Transthyretin Amyloidosis.
evidence.snippet: vutrisiran (siRNA) and inotersen (ASO) have all been licensed for treatment of ATTR-PN

nodes.description: Tongue enlargement from amyloid infiltration is a relatively specific physical finding for AL amyloidosis.

evidence.reference_title: Gastrointestinal manifestations of amyloidosis.
evidence.snippet: Gastrointestinal symptoms included anorexia, macroglossia, intestinal

nodes.description: NTLA-2001 (nexiguran ziclumeran) is an investigational, single-infusion lipid-nanoparticle CRISPR-Cas9 therapy designed to disrupt TTR in hepatocytes and durably lower circulating TTR. First-in-human evidence establishes target engagement in a very small cohort, not clinical efficacy.
nodes.id: NTLA-2001 in vivo TTR gene editing

evidence.reference_title: CRISPR-Cas9 In Vivo Gene Editing for Transthyretin Amyloidosis.
evidence.snippet: In a small group of patients with hereditary ATTR amyloidosis with polyneuropathy, administration of NTLA-2001 was associated with only mild adverse events and led to decreases in serum TTR protein concentrations through targeted knockout of TTR.

nodes.description: Glomerular amyloid deposition produces heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, edema, and nephrotic syndrome, typical of AL and AA amyloidosis.

evidence.reference_title: [Amyloidosis AA].
evidence.snippet: Nephropathy is the main clinical manifestation of amyloidosis.

evidence.reference_title: Renal involvement in AA amyloidosis: clinical outcomes and survival.
evidence.snippet: Mean serum creatinine and proteinuria at diagnosis were 4.65±4.89 mg/dl and 8.04±6.09 g/day

nodes.description: Lipid-nanoparticle-formulated small interfering RNA that silences hepatic TTR mRNA, lowering circulating transthyretin and slowing hereditary ATTR polyneuropathy progression.

evidence.reference_title: Patisiran, an RNAi Therapeutic, for Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis.
evidence.snippet: In this trial, patisiran improved multiple clinical manifestations of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis.

nodes.description: Length-dependent sensorimotor and small-fiber peripheral neuropathy is a hallmark of hereditary ATTR amyloidosis and can also occur in AL disease.

evidence.reference_title: Familial amyloid polyneuropathy.
evidence.snippet: TTR FAP typically causes a nerve length-dependent polyneuropathy that starts in the feet with loss of temperature and pain sensations, along with life-threatening autonomic dysfunction

nodes.description: Disease-specific precursors leave their native conformations and self-associate into beta-sheet-rich oligomeric and prefibrillar species. Soluble species can be proteotoxic, but the magnitude and organ specificity of that toxicity vary by precursor and are not assumed to be uniform.

evidence.reference_title: Transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis: clinical spectrum, molecular pathogenesis and disease-modifying treatments.
evidence.snippet: TTR protein destabilised by TTR gene mutation is prone to dissociate from its native tetramer to monomer, and to then misfold and aggregate into amyloid fibrils

evidence.reference_title: First-in-Human Phase I/II Study of NEOD001 in Patients With Light Chain Amyloidosis and Persistent Organ Dysfunction.
evidence.snippet: Light chain (AL) amyloidosis is caused by the accumulation of misfolded proteins, which induces the dysfunction of vital organs.

nodes.description: Glomerular amyloid deposition in AA amyloidosis produces proteinuria and progressive decline in renal function, the dominant clinical presentation.

evidence.reference_title: AA Amyloidosis: A Contemporary View.
evidence.snippet: emergence of proteinuria and gradual reduction in kidney function, apparent in over 90% of patients upon their initial presentation

evidence.reference_title: AA Amyloidosis: A Contemporary View.
evidence.snippet: serum AA (SAA) protein, through a long process including cleavage, misfolding, and aggregation into an insoluble beta-sheet form

nodes.description: In AA amyloidosis, persistent inflammation maintains the hepatic acute-phase response and chronically elevates serum amyloid A, supplying the precursor from which AA fibrils are formed.
nodes.id: Sustained Serum Amyloid A Precursor Production

evidence.reference_title: [Amyloidosis AA].
evidence.snippet: A permanent acute phase response, ideally evaluated with serial measurement of serum protein SAA, the precursor of the AA protein deposited in tissues, seems to be a prerequisite to the development of inflammatory (AA) amyloidosis.

evidence.reference_title: Familial amyloid polyneuropathy.
evidence.snippet: The first identified cause of FAP-the TTR Val30Met mutation-is still the most common of more than 100 amyloidogenic point mutations identified worldwide.

evidence.reference_title: The genetics of cardiac amyloidosis.
evidence.snippet: Over 150 different pathologic point mutations within the transthyretin gene have been identified, each carrying variable clinical phenotypes and penetrance.

evidence.reference_title: Prevalence, Cardiac Phenotype, and Outcomes of Transthyretin Variants in the UK Biobank Population.
evidence.snippet: The overall prevalence of LP/P variants was 0.02% (105 of 444 243) in participants with European ancestry and 4.3% (321 of 7533) in participants with African ancestry.

nodes.description: In ATTRv, pathogenic TTR variants destabilize the circulating tetramer; in ATTRwt, age-associated destabilization occurs without a pathogenic coding variant. Tetramer dissociation releases monomers that can misfold.
nodes.id: TTR Tetramer Destabilization and Monomer Release

evidence.reference_title: Transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis: clinical spectrum, molecular pathogenesis and disease-modifying treatments.
evidence.snippet: TTR protein destabilised by TTR gene mutation is prone to dissociate from its native tetramer to monomer, and to then misfold and aggregate into amyloid fibrils

nodes.description: Oral transthyretin tetramer stabilizer that binds the thyroxine-binding sites of TTR and prevents dissociation into amyloidogenic monomers. The pivotal ATTR-ACT trial established benefit in ATTR cardiomyopathy; regulatory indications for polyneuropathy vary by jurisdiction.

evidence.reference_title: Tafamidis Treatment for Patients with Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: In patients with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, tafamidis was associated with reductions in all-cause mortality and cardiovascular-related hospitalizations and reduced the decline in functional capacity and quality of life as compared with placebo.

nodes.description: Anti-interleukin-6 receptor monoclonal antibody used in AA amyloidosis to suppress the inflammatory drive of serum amyloid A production, lowering SAA and improving renal function.

evidence.reference_title: AA Amyloidosis: A Contemporary View.
evidence.snippet: tocilizumab was superior to anti-TNFs in terms of obtaining a decrease in SAA

nodes.description: Subcutaneous GalNAc-conjugated small interfering RNA that silences hepatic TTR mRNA. It lowers variant and wild-type TTR and has randomized phase III outcome evidence in ATTR cardiomyopathy as well as an indication for hereditary ATTR polyneuropathy.

evidence.reference_title: Vutrisiran in Patients with Transthyretin Amyloidosis with Cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: Among patients with ATTR-CM, treatment with vutrisiran led to a lower risk of death from any cause and cardiovascular events than placebo and preserved functional capacity and quality of life.
